significance: One of the oldest and most important Bhadrakali temples in Kerala and a principal centre of the state's goddess worship, best known for the Bharani festival. Its date of foundation is not established, though tradition ties it to the Sangam age.
story: It is told that after Parashurama raised Kerala from the sea the demon Darikan terrorised the land until Bhadrakali sprang from Shiva's three eyes and destroyed him; another tradition identifies the goddess here with Kannaki of the Tamil epic.
